items.title: Practising What Is Taught, Delegating to a More Fitting Teacher, and Both Together — Closing All Twenty-Seven Means

items.zh: 自成熟者，謂自宣說隨順正法，令諸有情出不善處，安立善處。如自所說，亦自修行法隨法行，令諸有情同分隨轉。勿使他人作如是說：汝自不能出不善處，安立善處，云何於他教授、諫舉、為作憶念？他應於汝教授、諫舉、為作憶念。
items.en: Self-ripening: teaching the true Dharma to lead beings out of unwholesome ground and establish them in wholesome ground — and, exactly as one teaches, personally practising that same teaching in accordance with the Dharma ... so that no one may rightly say: "You yourself cannot leave unwholesome ground and stand on wholesome ground — how then can you teach, correct, or remind others?"

items.zh: 請他成熟者，謂若有餘無量有情，於彼發起上品愛敬；或復有餘善知方便，於說正法已善修學；即應勸請慇懃營助，令其成熟無量有情。俱成熟者，謂具二種。若自成熟，若勸請他令其成熟。
items.en: Requesting another's ripening: when countless beings have already developed the deepest devotion and respect towards some other teacher, or when that teacher is especially skilled in expounding the true Dharma and has thoroughly mastered its practice, one earnestly requests and assists that teacher in ripening those countless beings. Both together: possessing both — ripening some beings oneself, while also inviting another to ripen others.

items.zh: 由此所說二十七種成熟方便，當知令前六種成熟差別圓滿。所謂諸根成熟、善根成熟、智慧成熟、下品成熟、中品成熟、上品成熟。云何能成熟補特伽羅？

items.title: Section: Six Kinds of Bodhisattva Who Ripen Others — And How Avalokiteśvara Received a Thousand Arms

items.zh: 謂略有六種菩薩，住菩薩六地，能成熟有情。一者、勝解行菩薩住勝解行地，二者、淨勝意樂菩薩住淨勝意樂地；三者、行正行菩薩住行正行地；四者、墮決定菩薩住墮決定地；五者、決定行正行菩薩住決定行正行地；六者、到究竟菩薩住到究竟地。
items.en: There are, in brief, six kinds of bodhisattva, abiding at six bodhisattva stages, who are able to ripen beings: first, the bodhisattva of resolute conviction, abiding at the stage of resolute conviction; second, the bodhisattva of pure, excellent aspiration, abiding at the stage of pure, excellent aspiration; third, the bodhisattva of genuine practice, abiding at the stage of genuine practice; fourth, the bodhisattva fallen into certainty, abiding at the stage of certainty; fifth, the bodhisattva of certain, genuine practice, abiding at the stage of certain, genuine practice; and sixth, the bodhisattva who has reached the end, abiding at the final stage.

items.title: Distinguishing Those Without a Fixed Lineage From Those With One

items.zh: 住無種姓補特伽羅，於往善趣而成熟時，有數退轉、有數應作。
items.en: A being with no fixed lineage, when ripened towards favourable rebirth, repeatedly falls back and repeatedly requires further guidance.

items.zh: 安住種姓補特伽羅，於往三乘而成熟時，無數退轉、無數應作。
items.en: A being settled in a genuine lineage, when ripened towards one of the three vehicles, no longer falls back, and once fully ripened, requires no further guidance at all.

items.zh: 云何已成熟補特伽羅相？

items.title: Section: The Marks of an Already-Ripened Hearer and Solitary Buddha — Three Grades Each

items.zh: 謂諸聲聞先已串習諸善法故，若時安住下品成熟，爾時便有下品欲樂、下品加行。猶往惡趣，非於現法證沙門果，非於現法得般涅槃。
items.en: Hearers who have cultivated wholesome practices in past lives, when abiding in inferior ripening, have inferior aspiration and inferior application. They may still fall into the lower realms, and neither attain the fruit of an ascetic's path nor reach final nirvāṇa in this present life.

items.zh: 若時安住中品成熟，爾時便有中品欲樂、中品加行。不往惡趣，於現法中證沙門果，非於現法得般涅槃。若時安住上品成熟，爾時便有上品欲樂、上品加行。不往惡趣，於現法中證沙門果，即於現法得般涅槃。如說聲聞，獨覺亦爾。何以故？道與聲聞同種類故。
而此獨覺與諸聲聞有差別者，謂住最後有、最後所得身，無軌範師，宿習力故，修三十七菩提分法，究竟斷滅一切煩惱，證阿羅漢，故名獨覺。
items.en: What distinguishes a solitary buddha from a hearer is this: dwelling in their final existence, in the very body in which they will attain the fruit, they have no teacher at all. Through the sheer power of past cultivation, they master the thirty-seven factors of awakening entirely on their own, thoroughly extinguish every affliction, and attain arhatship — hence the name "solitary" awakened one.

items.title: Section: The Marks of an Already-Ripened Bodhisattva — Three Grades Across Three Incalculable Eons

items.zh: 若諸菩薩住勝解行地，名下品成熟；住淨勝意樂地，名中品成熟；住墮決定、到究竟地，名上品成熟。若時菩薩住下品成熟，爾時便有下品欲樂、下品加行。猶往惡趣。此盡第一無數劫邊際，熾然、無動、極善清淨覺品善法，當知一切皆未相應。若時菩薩住中品成熟，爾時便有中品欲樂、中品加行。不往惡趣。此盡第二無數劫邊際，熾然、無動覺品善法已得相應，極善清淨覺品善法未得相應。
items.en: When a bodhisattva abides in inferior ripening ... a lower rebirth is still possible. This spans the boundary of the first incalculable eon, and one is not yet aligned with any of the blazing, unshakeable, and utterly pure factors of awakening. ... When a bodhisattva abides in middling ripening ... a lower rebirth is no longer possible. This spans the boundary of the second incalculable eon; the blazing and unshakeable factors of awakening are now aligned, though the utterly pure factors are not yet.

items.zh: 若時菩薩住上品成熟，爾時便有上品欲樂、上品加行。不往惡趣。此盡第三無數劫邊際，熾然、無動、極善清淨覺品善法，當知一切皆悉成就。今於此中，性淳厚故，極猛盛故，能有上品廣大果故，大勝利故，名為熾然。不轉還故，不退墮故，常勝進故，名為無動。
items.en: When a bodhisattva abides in superior ripening ... a lower rebirth is no longer possible. This spans the boundary of the third incalculable eon, and all of the blazing, unshakeable, and utterly pure factors of awakening are now completely accomplished. ... Here, because their character has grown genuinely settled, because their vigour blazes forth without restraint, because this yields a superior, vast fruit, and because it brings truly great benefit, this is called blazing. Because it never turns back, never regresses, and constantly advances, this is called unshakeable.

items.title: "Utterly Pure" — The Quality Found Only at the Very Highest Ground

items.en: This should be understood as what is called utterly pure.

items.title: Section: Nine Grades, and Ultimately Infinite Variation in How Beings Actually Ripen

items.zh: 當知此中，若財攝受所作成熟、若神通引攝所作成熟、若隱密說法所作成熟、若下品加行所作成熟、若唯聽聞所作成熟，如是五種所作成熟，若於長時修習彼法，尚為下品，況於少時修習彼法。
items.en: It should be understood that ripening accomplished through material attraction, through guidance by miraculous power, through teaching with hidden meaning, through inferior application, or through hearing alone — these five kinds of ripening remain inferior even if that method is practised for a long time, let alone practised only briefly.

items.zh: 其餘一切成熟因緣所作成熟，當知皆有三品道理。謂若於彼下品修習，成下成熟；中品修習，成中成熟；上品修習，成上成熟。
此下中上三品成熟，當知一一復有三品。於下品中，有下下、下中、下上三品成熟；於中品中，有中下、中中、中上三品成熟；於上品中，有上下、上中、上上三品成熟。如是等類諸佛菩薩成熟有情，當知展轉差別道理有無量品。
items.en: Each of these three grades of ripening — inferior, middling, and superior — should be understood to itself contain three further grades. ... The way buddhas and bodhisattvas ripen beings, in all these ways just described, should be understood to admit, when distinguished in full, truly boundless gradations.

items.title: Section: Fascicle 37 Complete — Ripening Oneself and Ripening Others, Closing the Chapter on Ripening

items.zh: 此中菩薩，由前所說成熟因緣，為欲成熟自佛法故，精勤修集諸根成熟、善根成熟、智慧成熟、下品成熟、中品成熟、上品成熟。
items.en: Here, bodhisattvas, by means of the causes and conditions of ripening already described, diligently cultivate the ripening of the faculties, of wholesome roots, and of wisdom, together with inferior, middling, and superior ripening, precisely in order to ripen their own buddha-qualities.

items.zh: 又欲令他諸有情類補特伽羅乘三乘法而出離故，往善趣故，修集如是六種成熟。
items.en: They also cultivate these same six kinds of ripening so that other beings may, riding whichever of the three vehicles fits them, be led out of suffering — or, lacking any fixed lineage, be led at least towards a favourable rebirth.

blocks.text: The last means of ripening, and the marks of those who are ripened. Fascicle 37 ends today. A short passage (0498a24) is untranslated.

"Teaching the Dharma to lead beings from unwholesome to wholesome ground, and, exactly as one teaches, practising it oneself", so that no one can say: "You yourself cannot leave unwholesome ground; how can you lead others?"
"When beings already trust another teacher, or that teacher is especially skilled", one asks that teacher to ripen them.
Bodhisattvas at six stages can ripen beings, from the stage of resolute conviction upwards. Master Cháng Bǎi tells a story about Avalokiteśvara's thousand arms.
"A being with no fixed lineage, ripened towards favourable rebirth, repeatedly falls back and requires guidance again." One with a fixed lineage, fully ripened, "requires no further guidance".

subs.head: Marks of ripened hearers and solitary buddhas

blocks.text: Inferior, middling, superior. Solitary buddhas "in their final existence have no teacher at all; through past cultivation, they master the thirty-seven factors on their own".

Inferior ripening spans the first incalculable aeon, when a lower rebirth is still possible; superior ripening, the third, when it is not, and the factors of awakening are "blazing, unshakeable, and utterly pure". Master Cháng Bǎi: only at the tenth ground is one "utterly pure".
Ripening by wealth, miracles, hidden teaching, inferior effort, or hearing alone "remains inferior, even if practised long". Each grade has three sub-grades: nine in all.
Power and ripening: what buddhas and bodhisattvas can do, and how they bring others to maturity. Fascicle 38 continues with the chapter on awakening (菩提品) and the perfections.

quiz.q: Self-ripening: "practice what you teach," lest one be told "you yourself can't … how can you teach?" What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: not practising oneself, one can't lead by example — and gets mocked
quiz.why: "Exactly as one teaches, personally practising that same teaching … so that no one may rightly say: 'You yourself cannot leave unwholesome ground … how then can you teach others?'" Master Cháng Bǎi: if you don't do it yourself or practice in accordance with the Dharma, you can't lead by example — and you'll be mocked in return.

quiz.q: Six kinds of bodhisattva ripen beings. In Master Cháng Bǎi's story of Avalokiteśvara's vow, what happened?
options: meant to shatter into a thousand pieces, he became thousand-armed and thousand-eyed — his vow grew vaster
quiz.why: "There are, in brief, six kinds of bodhisattva, abiding at six bodhisattva stages, who are able to ripen beings." Master Cháng Bǎi tells of Avalokiteśvara's vow that his head would shatter into a thousand pieces if he lost the resolve: what should have shattered into a thousand became a thousand arms and eyes, making his vow vaster.

quiz.q: Solitary buddhas "without a teacher … attain arhatship — hence 'solitary.'" What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: awakening without a teacher — hence "solitary," also called pratyekabuddha
quiz.why: "They have no teacher at all. Through the sheer power of past cultivation, they master the thirty-seven factors of awakening entirely on their own … and attain arhatship — hence the name 'solitary' awakened one." Master Cháng Bǎi: because they awaken without a teacher they're called solitary awakened ones, also pratyekabuddhas.

quiz.q: A bodhisattva of inferior ripening "may still fall into lower realms." Why, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: if he didn't go guide beings, he himself would have no problem
quiz.why: "When a bodhisattva abides in inferior ripening ... a lower rebirth is still possible." Venerable Miào Jìng, using Kuījī's image of the garuḍa whose feet get muddy catching nāgas: if he didn't go out to guide beings, he himself would have no problem.

quiz.q: "Constantly advancing — called unshakeable." What image does Master Cháng Bǎi use?
options: all wholesome qualities like the waxing moon from the 1st to the 15th
quiz.why: "Because it never turns back, never regresses, and constantly advances, this is called unshakeable." Master Cháng Bǎi: all wholesome qualities are like the waxing moon from the first to the fifteenth.

quiz.q: "This is called utterly pure." At which ground, per the masters?
options: Cháng Bǎi: before the tenth ground it's "purified"; Miào Jìng: the tenth ground is "utterly pure aspiration"
quiz.why: "This should be understood as what is called utterly pure." Master Cháng Bǎi: before the tenth ground, bodhisattvas can all be called "well purified." Venerable Miào Jìng: the tenth ground is called utterly pure aspiration. (The treatise's reason, "being highest among the bodhisattva grounds," is missing from the English.)

quiz.q: Ripening "through hearing alone" stays inferior even over a long time. What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: of hearing, reflection, and cultivation — hearing alone isn't enough
quiz.why: "Ripening accomplished … through hearing alone — these five kinds of ripening remain inferior even if that method is practised for a long time." Master Cháng Bǎi: of the three wisdoms of hearing, reflection, and cultivation, only hearing the Dharma isn't enough.
